headline: A film of the Odyssey fills cinemas

sources.title: Box Office: 'The Odyssey' Soars to $652 Million Globally After Two Weekends, Including $140 Million in Imax
'The Odyssey' extends stay in 70mm Imax theaters as shows sell out weeks in advance
Coveted 'The Odyssey' IMAX 70mm Screenings Extended After Weeks Of Sold Out Showings

chunks.text: The Odyssey is a Greek [[poem]] about 2,800 years old. A film of it has become the biggest cinema story of the summer. It {{came out}} on July 17, [[directed]] by Christopher Nolan with Matt Damon as Odysseus, and had {{raked in}} about 652 million dollars [[worldwide]] after only two weekends. About 140 million of that came from IMAX screens alone, which is unusual, because IMAX normally {{makes up}} a small [[share]] of any film's [[earnings]].

chunks.text: The reason is the way it was filmed. This is the first full length film [[shot]] entirely on IMAX film cameras, using more than two million feet of [[70mm]] film. Those cameras are heavy, noisy and rare, so most directors {{stay away from}} them and film [[digitally]] instead. The reward is a picture with far more detail than an ordinary cinema image, and one that fills a tall screen from top to bottom rather than filling only a wide strip across the middle.

verbs.wrong: To be unable to pay for something

chunks.text: The problem is that hardly anywhere can show it that way. Only about 25 cinemas in the whole United States can [[project]] 70mm IMAX. Seats at those [[screenings]] {{sold out}} as much as seven weeks ahead. One cinema [[chain]] had to {{set up}} a digital [[waiting list]] on its app when new tickets were released. Some people flew hundreds of miles to reach a screen. On July 30 the [[studio]] {{gave in}} to the [[demand]] and [[extended]] the 70mm [[run]] by a month, to September 16.

verbs.wrong: To be offered for sale early
To make a system work faster
To turn down a request politely

chunks.text: The money is not really the interesting part. A story that people have been {{passing down}} since before writing was common has {{filled up}} cinemas in 2026, and the reason [[audiences]] {{lined up}} was to see it in the oldest [[format]] available rather than the newest one. Whether other studios now {{take up}} film cameras again is a separate question, and an expensive one, because only a handful of these cameras exist anywhere in the world.
